1.note: For some languages it may be necessary to make it explicit that the boat was completed before Yahweh told Noah to enter it. Alternate translation: [Then after they had finished building the ark, Yahweh told Noah] or [After the ark was finished, Yahweh told Noah]
See how you translated **ark** in Genesis 6:14–16. Alternate translation: [Board the ark along with your entire family] or [You and your entire family must get into the ark]
Alternate translation: [because I have found] or [because I see]

In the Hebrew text, the pronoun **you** is emphasized to show that Noah was the only one who was righteous. See how you translated **righteous** in Genesis 6:9. Alternate translation: [that you alone are upright] or [that you are the only one who is living the right way]
Alternate translation: [in my eyes] or [according to my will]
For some languages it may be more natural to put this phrase earlier in this verse, after “because.” Alternate translation: [among the people living today]

2.note: Alternate translation: [From every kind of animal that is acceptable to sacrifice]
The pronoun **you** is singular in the Hebrew text, but could be translated as a plural to include Noah’s family. Alternate translation: [bring with you]
See how you translated “male and female” in Genesis 6:19.
Alternate translation: [and from every kind of impure animal] or [and from every kind of animal that is not acceptable to sacrifice]

3.note: Alternate translation: [from every type of bird that flies in the sky] or [from every type of bird]
See how you translated a similar phrase in verse 2. Also, for some languages it may be better to put this phrase earlier in the sentence, as in the UST.
Alternate translation: [so that later they will have offspring that will live]
Alternate translation: [and spread all over the earth] or [to repopulate the whole earth]

4.note: The word translated as **because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [The reason you must do so is that]

The phrase **seven more days** could be translated as “another week” here and in verse 11. However, it is probably best to keep the number seven in the text in both places, especially since the number seven often signifies perfection or completion in the Bible, perhaps also here. Alternate translation: [seven days from now]
This phrase refers to 40 complete 24-hour days.
See how you translated this common expression in 6:7. Alternate translation: [in order to blot out] or [That will wash away]
See how you translated a similar phrase **living creature** in Genesis 6:19. Alternate translation: [all the living things that I have made]

It may be clearer to put this phrase earlier in the sentence and say, “in order to completely destroy from the ground every living creature that I have made.” See how you translated this phrase in Genesis 6:7. Alternate translation: [off the surface of the earth] or [off the land]

5.note: Alternate translation: [So Noah did everything that] or [So Noah did everything just as]
See how you translated 6:22, which is similar to 7:5. Alternate translation: [Yahweh had told him to do]

6.note: See how you handled large numbers in [Genesis 5](ta:05) and in Genesis 6:3, and see the note about this at Genesis 5:35. Also see how you translated the common expression “son of … years” in Genesis 5:32. Alternate translation: [He was 600 years old]

For some languages it may be more natural to put this clause first in this sentence and say, “When the flood waters came on the earth, Noah was 600 years old.” Also, see how you translated **floodwaters** in Genesis 6:17. Alternate translation: [when the earth was covered with deep water]

7.q: וַ⁠יָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠⁠בָנָי⁠ו וְ⁠אִשְׁתּ֧⁠וֹ וּ⁠נְשֵֽׁי־בָנָ֛י⁠ו אִתּ֖⁠וֹ אֶל־הַ⁠תֵּבָ֑ה
7.note: Noah and his family entered the ark on the same day that the floodwaters started coming (See verses 7:11–13). See how you translated a similar list of people in Genesis 6:18. Alternate translation: [That is when Noah and his wife, and his sons and their wives, went together into the ark]
Alternate translation: [because of] or [to escape from] or [to keep them safe from]

8.note: Here, **and everything that moves on the ground** could (1) include every kind of creature that moves on land. Alternate translation: [which includes every kind of animal that lives on land] According to this interpretation, the rest of verse 8 emphasizes that the clean and unclean animals and birds (verses 2–3, 8) were all creatures that lived on land (which are the creatures that the flood affected). (2) refer to every kind of creature that crawls along the ground. According to that interpretation, the rest of verse 8 refers to a fourth category of creatures besides the clean animals, unclean animals, and birds.

8.q: מִן־הַ⁠בְּהֵמָה֙ הַ⁠טְּהוֹרָ֔ה וּ⁠מִן־הַ֨⁠בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵינֶ֖נָּ⁠ה טְהֹרָ֑ה
8.note: See how you translated **clean** and “unclean” animals in verse 7:2. Alternate translation: [Also, every kind of clean animal and every kind of unclean animal]

9.note: Alternate translation: [came to Noah in pairs and went into the ark] or [came in pairs and entered the ark with Noah]
Alternate translation: [Each pair had one male and one female]
Alternate translation: [which was exactly what God had told Noah to bring along]

10.note: This phrase focuses attention on an important event, the beginning of the flood. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event. Alternate translation: [Now it came about]

This phrase refers to the seven days which God talked about in verse 4. It does not mean seven days after Noah and the animals went into the ark (verses 7–9); they went into the ark on the same day that the flood started (verse 13). Translate the beginning of this sentence in a way that makes that clear. Alternate translation: [after seven days]
Alternate translation: [the floodwaters started to come on] or [water started to cover]

11.note: Compare how you translated Noah’s age in verse 7:6.
For some languages it is more natural to switch the phrase order and say which day it is before giving the month. Do what is natural in your language.
Alternate translation: [on that same day] or [that is the day when]
Alternate translation: [all the underground water sources]

For some languages it may be more natural to put this phrase earlier and say, “water started gushing out of all the fountains in the deep ocean,” Alternate translation: [split open] or [started gushed forth water]

The author is speaking of **the heavens** as if they had **windows** that **were opened** to describe the beginning of a very heavy rainfall; it does not refer to actual windows. Alternate translation: [and all the windows in the sky were opened by God] or [God also caused the water in the heavens to start coming down, as if he had opened huge faucets in the heavens]

12.note: Alternate translation: [so that heavy rain poured continuously]
See how you translated this phrase in verse 7:4.

13.note: This is the same day that is mentioned in verse 11, when the flood started. Verses 13–16 repeat what happened, in order to emphasize it. Make sure that a translation does not sound like this is the second (or third) time that Noah and his family and the animals entered the ark. Alternate translation: [So it was that on the very same day that the rain started]

13.q: נֹ֔חַ וְ⁠שֵׁם־וְ⁠חָ֥ם וָ⁠יֶ֖פֶת בְּנֵי־נֹ֑חַ וְ⁠אֵ֣שֶׁת נֹ֗חַ וּ⁠שְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת נְשֵֽׁי־בָנָ֛י⁠ו אִתָּ֖⁠ם
13.note: See how you translated a similar sentence in verse 7:7. Alternate translation: [Noah and his wife and their sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their three wives all]

14.note: Alternate translation: [They took with them every]
Alternate translation: [every kind of tame animal]

This clause could refer to (1) every other kind of animal that lives on the earth, which seems to fit this context best; (2) every kind of creature that crawls on the ground. Alternate translation: [and every kind of creature that crawls on the ground]

This phrase probably refers not only to birds, but also to other creatures that have wings and fly, such as bats and insects. Alternate translation: [and every kind of bird and everything else that has wings] or [and every kind of bird and every other kind of creature that flies]

15.note: See how you translated a similar clause in verse 7:9. Alternate translation: [They came to Noah and came into the ark] or [They entered the ark with Noah]
The word **flesh** refers here to any kind of creature or animal. Alternate translation: [pairs of every kind of animal] or [pairs of every kind of living thing]

See how you translated this phrase in Genesis 6:17. For some languages it may be better to change the order of the clauses in this verse and say, “Pairs of every kind of living thing that breathes air came to Noah and went into the boat.”

16.note: Consider whether it is better in your language to use **went** or “came” here. Also consider again how you translated **went** in verses 7, 9, 13, and 15. Alternate translation: [The pairs that came into the ark] or [Those animals]
See how you translated **all flesh** in verse 7:15. Alternate translation: [of every kind of creature] or [of every kind of living thing]
See how you translated “just as God commanded him” in verse 7:9. Alternate translation: [which was exactly what God had commanded him to bring along]
Alternate translation: [After that, Yahweh shut them in the ark] or [Then after they were all inside, Yahweh shut the door of the ark behind him]

17.note: Some translations begin this sentence without a conjunction. Do what is natural in your language. Also, notice that verses 7:17–20 talk about the forty days and nights that the flood kept getting deeper and deeper. Alternate translation: [After that the floodwaters kept getting deeper and deeper] or [The water kept coming]

For some languages it may be more natural to put this time phrase first in this sentence and say, “For forty days and forty nights the flood kept getting deeper and deeper all over the earth,” Also see how you translated this phrase in verse 7:12. Alternate translation: [for 40 days and 40 nights]
Alternate translation: [and as the water level rose] or [As the water got deeper and deeper]
Alternate translation: [it lifted up the ark so that it floated on the water high above the earth] or [it made the ark rise up off the ground and float]

18.note: Verse 18 repeats some of verse 17 to emphasize what happened. Consider what is the best way to begin this sentence in your language. Alternate translation: [So the floodwaters continued to rise and get much higher] or [Yes, the water continued …] or [The water continued …]
Alternate translation: [but the ark floated safely] or [so that the ark moved about]
Alternate translation: [on the surface of the water] or [on top of the water]

19.note: Alternate translation: [At last, the waters became very deep over the world, so that] or [Eventually the water became so deep on the world that]

For some languages it is better to use an active form of the verb here and say, “Eventually the water became so deep on the earth that it even covered all the highest mountains under the entire sky.” Alternate translation: [were covered by water] or [were submerged in water]

20.q: חֲמֵ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ מִ⁠לְ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה גָּבְר֖וּ הַ⁠מָּ֑יִם
20.note: See how you translated **cubits** in Genesis 6:15–16. Alternate translation: [In fact, the highest mountain tops were covered by at least twenty-two feet of water]
See how you translated **were covered** in verse 19. Alternate translation: [so that they were completely covered with water] or [… completely submerged in water] or [… completely under water]

21.note: This phrase refers to everything listed in verse 21, including people. See how you translated this phrase in Genesis 6:17. Alternate translation: [Then all the beings] or [Then every creature] or [Then every living thing]
Alternate translation: [that moved on the ground]
See how you translated this common expression in Genesis 6:17. Alternate translation: [breathed out its last breath] or [perished]
Alternate translation: [including all the birds, the tame animals]
Alternate translation: [including every kind of animal that lived in large numbers on the earth]
Alternate translation: [in addition to all the human beings]

22.note: See how you translated a similar phrase in verse 7:15. Alternate translation: [Every living thing that breathed air]
Alternate translation: [and was on dry land died]

23.note: See how you translated this common expression in verse 7:4. Alternate translation: [That is how Yahweh washed away] or [In that way, Yahweh blotted out]
See how you translated this phrase in verse 7:4. Alternate translation: [every living creature] or [all living things]
See how you translated **the surface of the ground** in verse 7:4. Alternate translation: [that was on the surface of the earth] or [that were on the land]
See how you translated **mankind** in verse 7:21. Alternate translation: [including all mankind]
Alternate translation: [and all the livestock and all the other animals that moved on the ground] or [and all the animals, including smaller animals that crawl on the ground]
Some languages leave out the phrase **of the sky** because it is not natural.

See how you translated “wipe … off” in verse 7:4. Alternate translation: [All of them were completely washed off the earth by God] or [He completely destroyed them all from the earth] or [Yes, God completely destroyed everything that lived on the earth]
Alternate translation: [so that only Noah was left alive, along with] or [so that the only ones who were left alive were Noah and] or [Only Noah survived, along with]
Alternate translation: [and the people and the animals that were with him in the ark]

24.note: Alternate translation: [Deep water continued to flood] or [The floodwaters stayed deep over]
See how you handled a large number in verse 7:6. Alternate translation: [the entire earth for 150 days]
